conviction_note: The findings genuinely offset (sum 0.0). Below-the-line items probably flatter headline EPS, and the stock trades at about 1.15x its cash. Against that, the company slipped its own milestones (no September update, Lessengers samples moved from Q2 to Q3) and the AI-optics peer read-through is mixed. The revenue bar is disputed ($0.5M to $3.1M), so p_up sits at 48 and abs_move at 9%, slightly above the 7.13% event-implied move, because this release is the first operating update since 13 Aug and there is no call to soften it.
bar: Revenue bar DISPUTED, so every size is capped small. Earnings Whispers: Q3 revenue $1.6M, EPS -$0.07 (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/POET). Benzinga: revenue $3.1M, EPS -$0.06. Stockalarm: revenue $0.5M, EPS -$0.08. MarketBeat: EPS -$0.07, one analyst (search summary). The EPS bar of about -$0.07 is agreed by two sources; revenue has no agreement. The company gives no numeric guidance, only 'substantial numbers of production units for qualification in the remaining quarters of 2026' (Q2 6-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001437424/000117184326005485/exh_991.htm) and a target of '>30,000 optical engine shipments across 2026' (company blog 2026-07-14). Q2 revenue was $569,925 against a $0.50M estimate.
positioning_check: Short interest about 23.1M shares, 13.3% of shares outstanding, 3.2 days to cover, falling 2.7% month on month (https://equibles.com/stocks/poet/summary, latest settlement; the sweep row has 14.0% of float with data through 2026-10-09). Merlin Trader puts 24.3M at 2026-09-30 and 23.7M (13.7%) at 2026-10-15. Elevated but not the 18-23% squeeze zone. Baseline: 25d skew +1.08 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 0.2 (call-heavy, retail; a Defiance 2x long ETF, POEL, exists), event-implied move 7.13%, straddle 14.43% over 7 days, ATM IV 122.7%. Run-up: -6.17% over 20 days, +0.49% over 5 days, -75% from the 52-week high, after a 30% October slide with no company news.

findings.finding: Q3 headline net loss is likely to come in well under the -$0.07 EPS consensus because of below-the-line items. Q2 net loss of $11.3M included $6.17M of finance advisory fees tied to the $400M May raise, $4.30M of other/interest income from only about six weeks of the $796M cash pile, and a $5.53M non-cash warrant fair-value gain. Q3 has a full quarter of interest on about $780M, likely lower advisory fees, and the stock fell 27% in Q3 ($10.28 at end-June to $7.48 at end-September), which pushes another warrant-liability gain. A Q3 loss of roughly -$0.02 to -$0.05 is plausible, against -$0.07.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 (13 Aug 2026) met the -$0.07 EPS bar exactly with revenue $570K against $500K, and the stock moved +0.45% (baseline row; StockTwits headline 'POET stock gains'). Earlier quarters missed EPS, and Q1's -11%/-22% around 14-15 May was dominated by the $400M offering, not EPS. The name has not traded on EPS.
findings.why_not_priced: Estimates cluster at -$0.06 to -$0.08, the same as Q2. If aggregators had modelled the full-quarter interest income on $796M and the advisory fees rolling off, the consensus would sit nearer -$0.03. The estimates come from one or two analysts and look carried forward.
findings.independence: Quarter-end prices come from a different source: Digrin monthly closes, June $10.28 and September $7.48 (https://www.digrin.com/stocks/detail/POET/price), with MarketBeat giving $7.48 on 2026-09-30. The P&L mechanics rest on the one Q2 6-K.

findings.finding: The stock trades at about 1.15x its cash. 173.04M shares at $5.12 make a market cap of $885.9M (stockanalysis, 2026-11-13), against $796.3M of cash and short-term investments at 30 Jun 2026, with no meaningful debt. After Q2-rate operating burn (-$12.2M) plus part of the $50M H2 capex program, Q3-end cash is likely about $750-780M, or roughly $4.35-4.50 per share. So the market values the operating business at about $100-130M, and a weak operating update has a cash-backed floor that a strong one does not cap.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print came with the stock this close to cash. At Q2 (Aug 2026) it traded around $8.56 against cash of about $4.60 per share and moved +0.45%.
findings.why_not_priced: The cash is public. What is not obvious is the asymmetry: a 30% October slide with no company news (Merlin Trader) took the stock near cash per share. If the market were pricing a symmetric outcome, the put skew would be visibly positive, and it is only +1.08.
findings.independence: Cash figure from the SEC 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001437424/000117184326005485/exh_991.htm); Merlin Trader has 173.1M shares and 78.7M warrants at 13 Aug (https://merlintrader.com/poet-technologies-company-hub/).

findings.finding: Pattern of milestone slippage going into the first operating update since 13 Aug. The Q2 release promised 'additional announcements and updates in September', but through 26 Oct no quantified shipment or qualification update appeared (the only September item is a 4 Sep CIOE exhibition notice). The Lessengers 1.6T 2xDR4 sample target moved from Q2 2026 (March release) to Q3 2026 (14 Jul FAQ) with no confirmation that samples shipped. The Q3 release, with no call, must now show whether the 800G production order (more than $5M, 'targeted for shipment in H2 2026') and qualification units actually shipped.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When an expected commercial milestone failed (the Celestial AI/Marvell PO cancellation, 27 Apr 2026), the stock fell about 47%. With no news in the promised September window, it fell 30% over 30 days into 18 Oct. Positive commercial news (Lumilens $50M PO, May 2026) drew +11%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the October slide is the market reacting to the silence. What is not priced is the release's actual shipment count. If the market expected a clean miss, skew would be bid and the stock would trade at or below cash; it trades about 15% above.
findings.independence: Company news page lists no release between 4 Sep and 16 Oct 2026 (https://poet-technologies.com/news.html). Q2 6-K promise (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001437424/000117184326005485/exh_991.htm). Lessengers slip in the company FAQ (https://www.poet-technologies.com/blog/faq-production-orders-cash-position-and-the-path-to-greater-revenue).

findings.finding: Peer read-through on 800G is mixed. Secondary summaries of Applied Optoelectronics' Q3 (5 Nov 2026) say 800G revenue (about $47.5M, nearly 4x sequential) came in slightly below expectations because LTA customers moved to 1.6T faster than planned, and that AAOI cut its end-2026 capacity target. A Chinese trade write-up of the same call reads 800G as stronger than expected. POET's only disclosed production order is for 800G engines, so a faster 800G-to-1.6T migration could delay its customers' 800G qualification.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for POET on peer prints specifically. Peers COHR, LITE and AAOI fell alongside POET in October (Merlin Trader). AAOI shares rose 6.9% after its print (Zacks via search).
findings.why_not_priced: A proxy: neither POET nor its customers have confirmed the effect. The peer printed after POET last spoke (13 Aug), so no POET estimate reflects it. Sources conflict, so it is small.
findings.independence: Proxy. Conflicting reading in C114 (https://m.c114.com.cn/w3542-1320631.html, 2026-11-06). AAOI release: https://finviz.com/news/417752/applied-optoelectronics-reports-third-quarter-2026-results

findings.finding: AI-optics demand read-through is strong. Lumentum (2 Nov 2026) reported FQ1'27 revenue of $1.26B (+136.5% y/y) and guided FQ2 to $1.575-1.625B, about $350M of sequential growth. That supports the demand backdrop for optical-engine and light-source suppliers after a sector-wide October sell-off.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: POET has moved with the AI-optics complex (fell with COHR, LITE and AAOI in October). No measured beta to peer prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced at sector level, since POET has not rebounded with peers (5-day run-up +0.49%). Transmission to a pre-revenue name depends on its own qualification. Macro-to-company proxy, so it is small.
findings.independence: Proxy. AAOI raised Q4 guidance to $385-420M (search summary of Zacks), which points the same way at sector level.

findings.finding: Lumilens, POET's largest prospective customer ($50M initial PO, framework of $500M+ over five years for EOI-based engines), came out of stealth on 6 Aug 2026 with more than $700M of new funding at a $5.51B valuation. It says it is shipping its scale-out product to a 'top hyperscaler' under a multi-billion-dollar agreement. That makes the counterparty to POET's anchor order credible and funded. POET is not named, and POET's EOI engineering samples are due late 2026, with production in 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Lumilens PO announcement (May 2026) moved the stock +11% intraday ('POET Technologies Rockets Another 11%', itiger).
findings.why_not_priced: Public before the Q2 release, and the stock has fallen since. Upside comes only if the Q3 release confirms EOI sample delivery or a Lumilens milestone. Revenue from the order depends on milestones (company FAQ).

findings.finding: CFO change two weeks before the print. Thomas Mika, CFO for ten years and a named defendant in the April 2026 securities class action over the disclosure of Celestial AI details, was replaced on 2 Nov 2026 by Giovanni Pacelli (ex-Silicon Labs Senior Director of Finance). Mika stays until 2 Dec. The Q3 release goes out under a CFO who started 14 days earlier, with no call, and quarterly calls only from Q4 (1 Mar 2027).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell 7.69% on 2 Nov 2026, the day of the CFO 6-K (baseline history row, session intraday).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced by the -7.7% on 2 Nov. The residual risk is a more conservative framing of shipments or capex in the first release under the new CFO. Without a call there is no chance to explain a soft quarter.

findings.finding: A $1M installment to Sanan for the remaining Super Photonics Xiamen interest was due 31 Oct 2026, and as of 2 Nov no company release or filing had confirmed payment. The Q3 release or its subsequent-events note may address it.
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial in dollars against $780M of cash. It matters only if it shows friction with a former JV partner.
findings.independence: None. Same Merlin Trader page as the milestone finding, a different fact.

outside_window.finding: Securities class action Jones v. POET Technologies (D.N.J.): lead plaintiffs appointed 2026-09-30. Early stage, no ruling scheduled in the window.
First quarterly conference call, with the new CFO, comes with Q4/FY2026 results on 2027-03-01. Lumilens EOI production ramp is targeted for 2027.

baseline_tension: The skew is balanced (+1.08) and the stock has already fallen 30% into the print and sits near cash, so the slippage negatives are largely in the price. Nothing found cuts strongly against the skew or the run-up, and p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 2 (one-offs below operating income): the EPS headline-beat finding rests on interest income and a warrant remeasurement, so it was cut from +0.5 to +0.3
Rule 5 (absence and proxies): the cash-floor asymmetry is an inference about the reaction, cut from +0.5 to +0.3; Lumentum demand proxy cut from +0.3 to +0.2

Rule 5 plus verification done after the freeze: the AAOI 800G read-through was cut from -0.6 to -0.2, because one source reads 800G as stronger than expected and the transmission is an unconfirmed proxy
Rule 1/3 (priced and caveat): the milestone-slippage finding was cut from -0.7 to -0.5, because the 30% October slide already reflects the missed September update
Rule 6 (disputed bar): revenue estimates range from $0.5M to $3.1M, so every finding stays capped under 1 point and p_up moves from 47 to 48

Lesson on untrustworthy history: tried to rebuild from confirmed releases and found only one clean print (Q2 +0.45%); abs_move left at 9 from the option-implied 7.13% plus first-update-since-August uplift
